html:
The Confederated Villages of Lisjan are an Ohlone people of the East Bay of San Francisco Bay, in present Oakland, Berkeley and the land around. They spoke Chochenyo.

In 1492 the East Bay was home to many small village groups, who lived on shellfish, acorns, fish and game and left large shell mounds along the bay shore. From 1797 the Spanish Mission San José drew them in, one of the Spanish missions in California, where disease and forced labour killed many. They have no federal recognition. In the 2010s the Lisjan leader Corrina Gould co-founded the Sogorea Te' Land Trust, which takes back land in the East Bay for Native use. Their neighbours included the Karkin to the north.
